sentences.text: 1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT PRAYING TO ALLOW THIS APPEAL BY SETTING ASIDE THE IMPUGNED JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 07.04.2016, PASSED IN MVC NO.60/2015, ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT-II AT YADGIRI.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted her arguments that respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The police authority has not complied the provisions of Section 158(6) of the MV Act.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding effective licence to drive the particular class of vehicle as on the date of the alleged accident.
Hence, sought for allow this appeal.

2. As against this learned counsel for the claimants/respondents has submitted his argument that the appellant/insurance company has not adduced any evidence before the tribunal to show that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having driving license at the relevant point of time.

Further he has submitted his argument that even this court presume that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having any driving license at the time of accident, then also in view of decision of Hon'ble Apex court reported in the case of Pappu & Ors vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, Insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and thereafter the insurance company can recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having regard to the facts and circumstances and in view of the submission of both counsel, the only point that arise for consideration is as follows:
1. Whether the tribunal has justified in not giving any finding as to the driving license of the offending vehicle?
2. What order?
4. My answer to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: As per final order 5. A perusal of the judgment of the tribunal in para 23, the tribunal has observed as under:
"23.
As such petitioner is entitled the compensation of Rs.1,95,800/-with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till realization of amount against the respondents.

In view of reasons on issue No.1 to 3 the said accident was taken place The Manager Shriram Genral Insurance ... vs Mallappa S/O Sanna Ningappa Manager And ... on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181469569/

sentences.text: 2 due to negligence of driver of auto and the vehicle of respondent No.2 was insured with respondent No.1 at the time of respondent No 1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable for payment of compensation.
Petitioner claims the compensation of Rs.9,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till realization of amount, but not produced any material to award such compensation.
So petitioner is entitled the compensation of. Rs. 1,95,800/-with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization amount against respondent No.1 & 2.
In view of above said reasons this court held issue No.4 in the affirmative."

6. Though the respondent has taken specific defence that Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation for violation of policy conditions, the tribunal has not observed anything as to the driving license of the offending vehicle.

7. A perusal of the charge sheet which is marked as Ex.P.2, it is crystal clear that after thorough investigation, the IO has submitted charge sheet against the accused for the commission of the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 IPC and Section 187 of MV Act and Section 3 R/w 181 of MV Act.
Charge sheet is produced by the claimant.
The claimants have not disputed the charge sheet submitted by the IO.
Therefore, that there are no evidence to discard the documentary evidence Ex.P.2 placed by the claimant.
Accordingly, respondents/Insurance company has proved that the driver of the vehicle was not having driving license at the relevant point of time.

8. The tribunal has passed an award that respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner but the tribunal has not passed any order on the principle of pay and recover.

That in view of judgment of Hon'ble Apex court reported in the case of Pappu & Ors vs.
Vinod Kumar Lamba & Another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, the claimants are entitled for the compensation from the Insurance company and Insurance company has to pay award amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in accordance with law.

sentences.text: Accordingly, Point No.1 is answer in partly Affirmative.

9. Point No.2: for the aforesaid reasons and discussion, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (1) The appeal is partly allowed.
(2) The order of tribunal is modified as under as to the liability of the Insurance company.

(3) The appellant/Insurance company shall pay the claim amount awarded by the tribunal to the appellant in the first instance with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle- respondent No.2 in accordance with law.
(4) Draw an award accordingly.
(5) Parties are directed to bare their own cost.
